sources.note: Contents only (Rosetta Project scan of the contents pages). Part Four (Tairora-Binumarien-Waffa) has phoneme chapters for Binumarien and Waffa but none for Tairora; the Tairora chapters are Vincent 'Notes on Tairora noun morphology' 530-546, Vincent 'Tairora verb structure' 561-587, McKaughan 'Sequences of clauses in Tairora' 588-597, Kerr 'Subject morphemes in the Tairora verb complex: Obura dialect' 598-624. The full volume is on archive.org as a lending-library scan only (languagesofeaste0000unse); search-inside is disabled for it.

sources.citation: Vincent, Lois E. & Anisi Kaave. 2010. Tairora-English Dictionary. Ukarumpa: Wycliffe Inc., PNG Branch. viii+642 pp. (Preface 'The sounds of Tairora' pp. v-vi; Appendix 'Grammar of Tairora' pp. 576-608, phonology introduction p. 578)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 650-page PDF (a full-text search for stress/accent/prominence returns only dictionary glosses). Phonology notes give segments only, plus vowel length ('The sounds i, a, and u are usually short while e, aa and o are long', p. 578) and two tonal minimal pairs: 'There is a tonal difference between the word for "man" vaiinti, and the word for "child" vainti' (p. 578) and 3pl reflexive 'nái (with different tone from singular)' (p. 583). North Tairora (Tairora/Kamunakira and Suwaira dialects).

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Tairora is mentioned only in the classification tables and Kenati lexicostatistics (pp. 473, 481); no Tairora phonology or suprasegmental sketch (the 'Suprasegmentals' paragraphs found are for Wiru and Kenati).

sources.citation: Bee, Darlene. 1965. Comparative and historical problems in East New Guinea Highland languages. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 4 (Pacific Linguistics A-6), 1-38.
sources.note: No statement about Tairora stress placement. The orthographic key (p. 7) includes a stress mark ('´ stress') and the 180 cognate sets cite Tairora forms from Vincent's lexical list with stress marked: mostly initial ('ake 'take', 'qete 'banana', 'kohe, 'aniro 'come', 'bairi 'dog', 'bate 'ground', 'kankare, 'quere, 'abundere..) but a minority with second-syllable stress (u'te 'bag', ra'bure 'daughter', tu'tuki 'fence', i'he 'fire', qi'ete 'head', bo'haiqa, ke'teri, ne'meri, u'bai, to'nebu). Bibliography (p. 37) lists Vincent, Alex R. & Lois 1962 'Tairora Phonemic Statement', TS (unpublished).
